topics.title: Basis of Charge & Conditions for Chargeability
explain: Income is taxed under Income from house property based on the annual value of building or land appurtenant thereto.
Three conditions must be satisfied: property must be building/land appurtenant, assessee must be the owner, and property must not be used for own business/profession.
Land appurtenant includes attached land like gardens or garages; vacant plot rent alone is taxed under PGBP or Other Sources.
Owner includes legal owner and deemed owners under Section 25 (e.g., transfer to spouse/minor child without adequate consideration, holder of impartible estate, buyer in possession u/s 53A TPA).
Business of letting commercial properties on rent is taxable as Business Income per Supreme Court ruling in Rayala Corporation (P) Ltd.

flow.title: Chargeability Test under Section 20
steps: Check if building or appurtenant land exists
Verify assessee is owner or deemed owner
Confirm property not used for own business
Tax annual value under House Property

topics.example: If Mr. A transfers a residential house to his wife without adequate consideration, Mr. A remains the deemed owner taxable under Section 20.
remember: Rent from letting out vacant plot of land is taxable under Other Sources or PGBP, never under House Property.
mistakes: Taxing sub-letting income under Income from House Property instead of Income from Other Sources.

quiz.q: Which head of income taxes rental income from letting out a vacant plot of land?
o: Income from Other Sources or PGBP
quiz.why: Vacant land without any building is taxed under Income from Other Sources or PGBP.

quiz.q: Under Section 25, a transfer of house property to a spouse without adequate consideration makes the transferor a:
quiz.why: Section 25 treats an individual transferring property to a spouse without adequate consideration as the deemed owner.

topics.title: Composite Rent & Taxability
explain: Composite rent is single rent received for building along with other assets (furniture, machinery) or services (lift, security, power backup).
If letting of building and other assets/services is separable, rental of building is taxed under House Property and remaining under PGBP or Other Sources.
If letting of building and other assets is inseparable, total composite rent is taxed under PGBP or Income from Other Sources.
Separability depends on whether the tenant accepts renting the building without the other assets.

flow.title: Tax Treatment of Composite Rent
steps: Receive composite rent for building and assets
Check if lettings are separable
If separable: split building and asset rent
If inseparable: tax full amount under PGBP/Other Sources

topics.example: Renting a flat with an option to rent only the building without furniture allows splitting rent between House Property and Other Sources.
remember: The key test for composite rent taxability is whether letting of building and assets is separable or inseparable.
mistakes: Taxing inseparable composite rent under Income from House Property instead of PGBP/Other Sources.

quiz.q: If letting out of building and furniture is inseparable, composite rent is taxable under:
o: PGBP or Income from Other Sources
quiz.why: Inseparable composite rent cannot be split and is taxed as business income or other sources.

quiz.q: When building rent and service charges (lift, security) are separable, building rent is assessed under:
quiz.why: Separable sum attributable to the use of property is assessed under Section 20.

topics.title: Income from Foreign House Property
explain: For Resident and Ordinarily Resident (ROR), income from house property situated outside India is taxable in India whether brought to India or not.
For Non-Resident (NR) or Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR), foreign property income is taxable in India only if received in India.
Foreign municipal taxes paid to local authorities in the foreign country are allowed as deduction from GAV.

flow.title: Foreign Property Taxability Flow
steps: Identify residential status of assessee
If ROR: global house property income taxable
If RNOR/NR: taxable only if received in India
Deduct local foreign municipal taxes paid

topics.example: A resident Indian owning a rented house in London includes net rental income in Indian tax return after deducting London municipal taxes.
remember: Foreign municipal taxes actually paid to foreign local authorities are deductible while computing NAV.
mistakes: Taxing foreign house property income of an RNOR when the rent is received outside India.

quiz.q: Income from house property situated outside India is taxable in India for a Non-Resident only if:
o: It is remitted to a foreign bank
quiz.why: Non-residents are taxed on foreign income only if it is received in India.

quiz.q: Are municipal taxes paid to local authorities outside India deductible from GAV?
o: Yes, fully deductible if paid by owner
quiz.why: Taxes levied by foreign local authorities are deductible as per judicial precedent (CIT v. R. Venugopala Reddiar).

topics.title: Determination of GAV and Municipal Taxes
explain: Expected Rent (ER) is higher of Municipal Value (MV) and Fair Rent (FR), restricted to Standard Rent (SR).
GAV of let-out property is higher of Expected Rent (ER) and Actual Rent received/receivable (excluding unrealized rent per Rule 21).
If actual rent is lower than ER purely owing to vacancy, actual rent received/receivable becomes GAV u/s 21(2).
Municipal taxes paid by the owner during the tax year are deducted from GAV to arrive at Net Annual Value (NAV).

flow.title: GAV and NAV Calculation Steps
steps: Compare MV and FR (take higher)
Restrict to SR to get Expected Rent
Compare ER with Actual Rent received/receivable
Determine GAV (accounting for vacancy u/s 21(2))
Deduct municipal taxes paid by owner for NAV

topics.example: If MV is 30,000, FR is 36,000, and SR is 28,000, ER is 28,000. If Actual Rent is 25,000 without vacancy, GAV is 28,000.
remember: Municipal taxes are deductible ONLY if borne and actually paid by the owner during the tax year.
mistakes: Deducting municipal taxes that are unpaid or paid by the tenant.

quiz.q: Expected Rent (ER) under Section 21(1)(a) is calculated as:
o: Higher of MV and FR, restricted to SR
Average of MV, FR and SR
quiz.why: Expected Rent is higher of Fair Rent and Municipal Value, subject to a maximum of Standard Rent.

quiz.q: Municipal taxes paid by tenant are:
quiz.why: Municipal taxes are allowable as deduction only if borne and paid by the owner.

topics.title: Deductions from Annual Value
explain: Section 22(1)(a) provides a flat standard deduction of 30% of NAV for let-out/deemed let-out properties.
Section 22(1)(b) allows deduction for interest on loans taken for acquisition, construction, repair, renewal, or reconstruction.
Pre-construction interest is deductible in 5 equal annual installments starting from the completion/acquisition year u/s 22(1)(c).
Under default tax regime u/s 202(1), NO interest deduction is allowed for self-occupied properties.

Under optional tax regime u/s 202(4), self-occupied interest deduction is capped at Rs 2,00,000 (acquisition/construction within 5 years + certificate) or Rs 30,000 (repairs/others) for up to two properties.

flow.title: Deductions u/s 22 Workflow
steps: Start with Net Annual Value (NAV)
Deduct 30% of NAV u/s 22(1)(a)
Calculate current year interest on loan
Add 1/5th pre-construction interest
Apply ceiling limits based on tax regime

topics.example: Interest of Rs 1,80,000 plus 1/5th pre-construction interest Rs 72,000 equals Rs 2,52,000, restricted to Rs 2,00,000 for self-occupied house under optional regime.
remember: Interest on let-out / deemed let-out property has NO ceiling limit under both tax regimes.
mistakes: Claiming interest deduction on penal interest / interest on unpaid interest, which is strictly not deductible.

quiz.q: Under the default tax regime u/s 202(1), interest deduction for self-occupied property is:
quiz.why: Under default tax regime, no deduction u/s 22 is allowed for self-occupied properties.

quiz.q: Pre-construction interest is allowable as deduction in how many equal annual installments?
quiz.why: Pre-construction interest is deductible in 5 equal installments starting from the completion year.

topics.title: Computation for Different Property Categories
explain: Self-Occupied / Unoccupied: Annual Value is Nil for up to 2 properties (Individual/HUF); no municipal tax deduction allowed.
Deemed Let-Out: If more than 2 properties are self-occupied, assessee chooses 2 as self-occupied (NAV=Nil); remaining are treated as deemed let-out with ER as GAV.
Stock-in-Trade u/s 21(5): Annual value of un-let stock-in-trade property is Nil up to 2 years from the end of FY in which completion certificate is obtained.
Let-Out Part Year & Self-Occupied Part Year u/s 21(7): ER for full year is compared with actual rent for let-out period; higher is GAV.
Area-wise Split: If a portion is let out and portion self-occupied, compute let-out and self-occupied units separately by apportioning values based on plinth area.

flow.title: Categorization & GAV Determination
steps: Check property usage category
If Self-Occupied (max 2): Annual Value = Nil
If Deemed Let-Out: GAV = Expected Rent
If Stock-in-Trade: Nil NAV for 2 years
If Area-wise split: Apportion MV/FR/Taxes

topics.example: A house with 2/3rd self-occupied area and 1/3rd let-out area is split into Unit I (self-occupied, NAV=Nil) and Unit II (let-out, GAV computed u/s 21(1)).
remember: Benefit of Nil Annual Value for self-occupied properties is restricted to maximum 2 residential houses.
mistakes: Apportioning actual rent received when splitting a house into self-occupied and let-out area units.

quiz.q: For house property held as stock-in-trade not let out, Annual Value is Nil for up to:
quiz.why: Section 21(5) provides Nil annual value benefit up to 2 years from the end of the financial year of completion.

quiz.q: How many self-occupied house properties can an Individual claim Nil Annual Value for?
quiz.why: Section 21(6) allows benefit of Nil Annual Value for up to two self-occupied properties.

topics.title: Arrears of Rent and Unrealized Rent Received Subsequently
explain: Arrears of rent or unrealized rent recovered subsequently are deemed to be house property income in the year of receipt/realization u/s 23(1).
Section 23(3) grants a statutory deduction of 30% of such arrears or unrealized rent recovered.
The recovered amount is taxable even if the assessee is no longer the owner of the house property in the year of receipt.

flow.title: Recovery of Rent u/s 23
steps: Receive arrears or unrealized rent
Identify receipt year as tax year
Deduct 30% standard deduction u/s 23(3)
Tax remaining 70% under House Property

topics.example: If Mr. A recovers Rs 10,000 unrealized rent after selling his house, taxable income under Section 23 is Rs 7,000 (Rs 10,000 less 30% deduction).
remember: Ownership of property in the year of receipt is NOT required to tax arrears or unrealized rent u/s 23.
mistakes: Forgetting to allow the 30% standard deduction on arrears of rent received.

quiz.q: What percentage of standard deduction is allowed on recovery of arrears of rent u/s 23(3)?
quiz.why: Section 23(3) provides a deduction of 30% of arrears of rent or unrealized rent realized.

quiz.q: Are arrears of rent taxable if the assessee is no longer the owner of the property in the receipt year?
o: Yes, taxable u/s 23 regardless of ownership
quiz.why: Section 23 explicitly taxes recovery even if the assessee is not the owner in the year of receipt.

topics.title: Treatment of Co-owned Property
explain: Where property is co-owned with definite and ascertainable shares, co-owners are not assessed as an AOP.
For let-out co-owned property, overall income is computed as if owned by a single owner, then apportioned among co-owners per their share.
For self-occupied co-owned property, annual value for each co-owner is Nil.
Under the optional tax regime, each co-owner of a self-occupied property can individually claim interest deduction up to Rs 2,00,000 / Rs 30,000.

flow.title: Co-owned Property Income Assessment
steps: Verify definite and ascertainable co-owner shares
If Let-Out: compute total income then split per share
If Self-Occupied: Annual value = Nil for each
Apply separate interest deduction limits per co-owner

topics.example: Two sisters co-owning a self-occupied house with Rs 5,00,000 total loan interest can each claim Rs 2,00,000 deduction under the optional regime.
remember: The ceiling limit of Rs 2,00,000 for self-occupied interest applies to EACH co-owner individually.
mistakes: Restricting the combined interest deduction of all co-owners to Rs 2,00,000 instead of allowing up to Rs 2,00,000 for each co-owner.

quiz.q: How are co-owners with definite shares assessed for let-out house property?
o: Assessed as an Association of Persons (AOP)
Income computed together then apportioned to each co-owner
quiz.why: Section 24 requires computing income as if owned by one owner and then apportioning it among co-owners.

quiz.q: Under optional tax regime, the maximum interest deduction for acquisition of a self-occupied co-owned property is:
o: Rs 2,00,000 in total for all co-owners
quiz.why: Each co-owner is separately entitled to the maximum deduction of Rs 2,00,000 for self-occupied property.
